novelty.justification: The claim hypothesizes that models "linearly encode the physical DIMENSION/unit-type ... separately from its numerical magnitude" but "fail to CONSULT this representation," so its novelty route is a specific representation–behavior relationship and internal measurement rather than merely the medication-dosing setting. Searches under "LLM internal representation physical units dimensions," "mechanistic interpretability dimensional analysis unit errors," "linear probe unit type language model," and "LLM knows but fails to use encoded information" point to behavioral unit/dosing evaluations such as Can Large Language Models Assist with Pediatric Dosing Accuracy? (2025), general linear-representation work such as Language Models Represent Space and Time (Gurnee and Tegmark, 2024), and standard probe/causal-intervention studies, but not an equivalent study of an abstract unit-type code or its non-consultation during dimensional errors. Moving from those works to the claimed "know-but-dont-check gap" is a substantive multi-step integration and new operationalized relationship, but it remains a natural extension of established probing, activation-patching, and latent-knowledge/error-monitoring paradigms rather than a new interpretability paradigm.
